title: Conjecture 4
statement_text: For any sufficiently large odd integer $k$, $m(C_k) = (k-1)!/2$.
context_text: The Ramsey number $r(H)$ is the minimum $n$ such that every two-coloring of the edges of $K_n$ contains a monochromatic copy of $H$, and the threshold Ramsey multiplicity $m(H)$ is the minimum number of monochromatic copies of $H$ over all two-edge-colorings of $K_{r(H)}$. Harary and Prins asked for the determination of $m(P_k)$ and $m(C_k)$; for odd cycles Rosta and Surányi proved $m(C_k)\ge 2^{ck}$ and Károlyi and Rosta $m(C_k)\ge k^{ck}$, and the authors prove that $m(C_k)\ge(ck)^k$ for every odd $k$ and some constant $c>0$. For $a,b\ge1$, let $\chi(a,b)$ be the red/blue coloring of $K_{a+b}$ with vertex set $A\cup B$, $|A|=a$, $|B|=b$, where $A$ and $B$ are blue cliques and all edges between them are red. For odd $k\ge5$, $\chi(k-1,k-1)$ shows $r(C_k)>2k-2$, and $\chi(k,k-1)$ is a coloring of $K_{2k-1}=K_{r(C_k)}$ with exactly $(k-1)!/2$ monochromatic copies of $C_k$, all in the blue clique of order $k$. This shows that the $(ck)^k$ bound is tight up to the value of $c$, and the authors conjecture that this coloring is optimal for large odd $k$. Their proof goes through a stability lemma: every two-edge-coloring of $K_{2k-1}$ either has a regularity partition whose reduced graph contains a long monochromatic path, or is close to $\chi(k,k-1)$.
paper_title: Threshold Ramsey multiplicity for odd cycles
